question: On a Fedora Workstation that has never seen a developer install, with SELinux enforcing and none of Cirrove's dependencies present beforehand, does installing the packages alone produce a working daemon, mount, tray and Files integration -- and does removing them leave nothing behind?
why_now: M6 line 321 asks for a fresh installation verified outside development on each declared distribution family, and names Fedora with SELinux enabled specifically. The Fedora VM has been checked before, but its kickstart listed fuse3, nautilus-python and gnome-shell-extension-appindicator in %packages -- exactly what the spec declares as Requires and Recommends. The machine already had everything the package was meant to ask for, so the check could not fail. The kickstart no longer lists them, which is what makes this run evidence rather than ceremony.
how: The Fedora 44 VM is reinstalled from the netinst image with the corrected kickstart (nothing Cirrove needs in %packages), then the two rpm packages CI built for the current tree are installed with dnf from a local file, so the dependency solver has to find everything else itself. The machine is driven over ssh and QEMU's monitor; the session is a real GNOME Wayland session with the test user logged in automatically. The previous disk is kept as disk-plasma-coverage-2026-09-13.qcow2, because it carries the Plasma evidence.

predictions.P1: Installing cirrove pulls in fuse3 through its Requires, and installing cirrove-desktop pulls in nautilus-python and gnome-shell-extension-appindicator through its Recommends, with no package named by hand beyond the two rpms. This is the clause the old kickstart made unfalsifiable, so it is the one most likely to be wrong.
predictions.P2: SELinux is enforcing, and the daemon starts, mounts and serves reads with no AVC denial mentioning cirrove. FUSE in a user unit under a confined-by-default policy is the plausible failure here; unconfined_t for user processes is the reason it may pass.
predictions.P3: After a reboot, with nothing started by hand, cirroved.service is active and the tray item is registered on the session bus and drawn in the GNOME top bar, and Files loads the extension from /usr/share/nautilus-python without a second copy anywhere.
predictions.P4: With no account signed in, the service reports zero accounts and no mount, and says so as a plain fresh state rather than as an error or a failure to start.
predictions.P5: Removing both packages leaves nothing package-owned on the machine: no binaries, no unit, no autostart entry, no Files extension, no icons, no desktop entry, no metainfo.
predictions.P6: The rpms are built as .fc42 and this is Fedora 44; they install and run anyway, because nothing in them links against a library whose soname moved between the two.

run.where: Fedora 44 Workstation, reinstalled from the netinst image this morning with the corrected kickstart; GNOME Wayland, autologin; packages 0.1.0~dev.r409.ge24da99 built by CI for the current tree

observed.P1: HOLDS for the Recommends, and cannot be shown for the Requires. Before installing, nautilus-python and gnome-shell-extension-appindicator were both absent. Installing the two rpms and naming nothing else brought in seven packages: the two of ours plus nautilus-python 4.1.0, gnome-shell-extension-appindicator 64, libappindicator-gtk3, libdbusmenu-gtk3 and libdbusmenu. So the desktop package's Recommends really do carry the Files extension and the GNOME tray support. fuse3 is the exception and the prediction was wrong about it being testable here: Fedora Workstation installs fuse3 3.18.2 as part of its own environment group, so it was already present and removing it from the kickstart changed nothing. A machine where fuse3 can be absent is the Ubuntu container in CI, and the headless install job now asserts it there.
observed.P2: HOLDS. getenforce reported Enforcing. No AVC denial mentioning cirrove appeared while the service and tray were started, nor after the reboot. The daemon started, and with no account there is no mount, so this says the service and tray run under the policy -- not yet that a FUSE mount does. That needs the sign-in.
observed.P3: HOLDS. After the reboot, with nothing started by hand, cirrove-tray was running from the packaged /etc/xdg/autostart entry, cirroved.service was active, and the tray item reported IconName io.github.Dandiccf.Cirrove-ready. Files loaded the extension from /usr/share/nautilus-python and logged it asking about three directories; exactly one copy is installed. desktop-file-validate passed both entries and appstreamcli validated the metainfo with one pedantic note.
observed.P4: HOLDS. accounts is the empty list, active_mounts is 0, and the tray's Status is Passive, which is why a shell hides the icon rather than showing a broken one. Nothing reported an error.
observed.P5: HOLDS. dnf remove took all seven packages, and a find over /usr and /etc for anything named cirrove returned nothing at all. ~/.local/state/cirrove was left in place, which is the intended answer: removing the package is not consent to delete the person's data.
observed.P6: HOLDS. The rpms are built .fc42 and installed and ran on Fedora 44 without complaint.

run.also_noticed: Immediately after installing, the running GNOME Shell did not know the appindicator extension existed -- gnome-extensions reported it does not exist, seconds after dnf installed it. A shell only scans for extensions at start, and on Wayland it cannot be restarted without ending the session. So on Fedora the tray cannot appear until the person logs out and in again, or reboots; after the reboot the tray was running and registered. That belongs in the user guide, because the person who installs the desktop package and looks at the top bar will see nothing and conclude it is broken.
run.not_covered: Sign-in, and therefore a mount. A Microsoft sign-in is the machine owner's browser and credentials, and they are not written down anywhere for a script to use. The sign-in-and-reboot half of M6 line 321 stays open, and with it the one SELinux question that matters most: whether a FUSE mount in a user session draws a denial. Everything above is what can be established without the owner.

sign_in_and_reboot.who: the account owner typed their Microsoft credentials at the VM's console; everything either side of that was driven from the host
sign_in_and_reboot.consent: read-only. Write consent was not requested: everything this run had to establish is reachable read-only, and the write path already has real evidence on the Ubuntu VM (192 applied changes). The mount enforces it -- files are -r-------- and touch in the mount returns Read-only file system.

observed.keyring: A fresh machine that logs in automatically has no keyring at all -- ~/.local/share/keyrings was empty and the Secret Service offered only a transient session collection, so a sign-in would have failed at the moment it stored the token. Autologin was turned off and the session logged into once with a password, which is the path the user guide already prescribes; login.keyring then existed and reported Locked=false. This is the fixture row in the compatibility table meeting a real machine.
observed.mount_under_selinux: HOLDS, and this was the open question. With SELinux Enforcing and the drive mounted, the whole boot carries zero AVC denials -- not zero mentioning cirrove, zero of any kind, by journalctl -b and by ausearch. A 67794-byte pptx read end to end through FUSE returns the correct PK zip magic and the byte count stat reports.
observed.desktop_surfaces: First time on Fedora with an account. The tray item goes from Passive to Active and the GNOME shell draws it in the top bar; Files shows OneDrive in its sidebar with an eject button; the pinned file carries Cirrove's own kept-offline badge and its on-demand neighbours carry none.
observed.reboot: HOLDS. After a reboot, with nothing started by hand, the account is present and mounted, the mount lists the drive, the pin survived with its 66 KB still resident, and the tray is Active again.

sign_in_and_reboot.also_noticed: cirrove connect asks which drive to mount on the terminal, so running it without a terminal -- which is how a desktop sign-in reaches it -- fails after the browser half has already succeeded, with 'cannot parse integer from empty string'. The sign-in was real and the token was thrown away. --drive-id avoids the prompt entirely. The error names an integer parse rather than the thing the person has to do.
sign_in_and_reboot.still_open: Arch. M6 line 325 asks for each declared distribution family, and the Arch package has never been installed on a clean Arch machine with a sign-in. Ubuntu and Fedora are now both evidenced.

conclusion: A Fedora Workstation that has never seen a developer install accepts the packages, brings its own desktop integration with them, runs under SELinux enforcing without a denial, comes back after a reboot from the packaged autostart, and removes without leaving a single file named cirrove behind. Five of the six predictions hold as written; the sixth was wrong in a way worth keeping -- fuse3 cannot be absent on Fedora Workstation, so the hard dependency is proven in CI's container instead, where the machine really does start without it. The sign-in half was then completed the same morning with the owner at the console: the drive mounts under SELinux enforcing with zero AVC denials of any kind, a real file reads end to end through FUSE, the tray goes Active and is drawn by the shell, Files shows the mount and the branded badge, and all of it survives a reboot with nothing started by hand. What stays open is Arch, which is a declared family with no clean-machine installation, and the GNOME extension's need for a fresh session before the tray can appear, which is a documentation gap rather than a defect.
